correctness.rationale: Removing an edge leaves exactly its endpoints and the old hole free, so a distinct replacement must join the hole to one of those endpoints; each of the 2m choices is legal and gives a distinct neighbor. The noncommon edges of two matchings split into alternating cycles and, if the holes differ, one even path. At least |M∖N| flips must insert missing target edges. The first deletion of a source edge of any original cycle must use the hole outside that cycle and insert a nontarget edge, giving one separate extra flip per cycle. Equality is attained by walking the hole along the path and then switching each cycle with the final hole as a pivot, using j+1 flips for j source edges on the cycle and returning the pivot to its initial location. Transitivity follows from relabeling. A path on k selected source blocks has 2^k k! choices; a j-block cycle has 2^(j−1)(j−1)! choices modulo rotation and reversal, including j=2. The labeled product with the unchanged blocks gives the exponential generating function; summing the logarithm gives the stated closed form, also normalized at z=1 to the number of possible matchings. Maximum distance uses all blocks and the largest possible number of cycles. For even m only 2-block cycles occur; for odd m the extra block either extends one cycle to three or forms the one-block path. These give the stated top coefficients; m=1 is the separate one-block-path case. Equal eccentricities give the same radius and diameter.
residual_risks: The saved BFS and component-enumeration runs agree through m=5 and were inspected, not rerun. The proof covers all m; the recorded tests do not establish all m by themselves.

evidence: Aichholzer et al. describe the same combinatorial flips for general graphs, alternating-path transport, and a j+1-flip switch when the hole is adjacent to a cycle. Their double-counting discussion at Theorem 15 identifies one extra flip per cycle. Lindzey's association scheme classifies pair types on the identical state space. Brenner et al. prove Hamilton-connectedness on the identical graph, a different invariant.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Completeness makes all adjacent-hole switches available, so the known component argument yields the exact t+c distance without solving any additional reachability problem. Hamilton-connectedness alone would not imply it.
searches: arXiv:1811.06160, §11, Theorem 56 and following association scheme, pp. 37–38

evidence: Fixing a source matching leaves a stabilizer of order 2^m m!. For the known orbital with path length 2k, a common edges, and b_j cycles of length 2j (j≥2), m=k+a+Σ j b_j. The joint stabilizer fixes the path pointwise, since the source hole specifies one endpoint, has order 2 on each common edge, and has 2j color-preserving symmetries on each 2j-cycle; copies of an identical component can be permuted. Thus the type has size 2^m m! / [2^a a! ∏(2j)^{b_j} b_j!]. The distance is k+Σ(j+1)b_j by the prior component-switch analysis in the complete graph. Summing these sizes with that distance as exponent and dividing by m! gives (1−2uz)^(-1) exp(u) exp(Σ_{j≥2} (2^{j−1}/j)u^j z^{j+1}), exactly the frozen series.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The weight on an orbital and its multiplicity are automatic from the established component metric and standard orbit stabilizer on the established orbital list. The geometric crossing-free theorem is supportive, but is not treated as an identity of geometric and combinatorial graphs: the combinatorial switches plus the cycle-entry lower count suffice. The EGF simplification and top-degree enumeration add no distinct theorem beyond this deterministic specialization.

evidence: 4215f72aa114 gives the same graph expressed as minimum dominating sets in the odd triangular graph, with the same t+c, EGF, radius/diameter and antipodal counts. For m≥2 a dominating set of m edges in the line graph must cover at least 2m of the 2m+1 underlying vertices (otherwise an uncovered pair yields an undominated edge), so these edges are exactly near-perfect matchings. Replacing a dominating-set vertex corresponds to a single-edge flip. The bipartite peer df80d3d712a4 uses K_(n,n) and a different metric.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The triangular-graph record is substantive exact equivalent coverage, but is dated later and is not used as earlier art. That equivalence is by the shared state graph, not just numerical matching. The decisive earlier implication comes from the primary results below.

originality.rationale: The result is correct, but the distance and the enumeration are mechanically implied by the earlier odd-matching flip analysis and the known near-perfect matching orbitals. Aichholzer et al. give the combinatorial path and cycle switches and identify the unavoidable cycle-entry overhead; on a complete graph every direct cycle entry is available. Lindzey already classifies the pair orbitals on the very same near-perfect matchings. Their distance weights and orbit sizes give the frozen EGF by a direct orbit-stabilizer sum, detailed below. Thus the closed form is not an independently distinct exact invariant under the review standard. No earlier explicit printing of the entire EGF was found; the later exact catalogue match is corroborating evidence about equivalence, not the basis for earlier coverage.
residual_risks: An earlier explicit printing of the EGF was not established; the failure is the demonstrable mechanical implication, not a claim about an identical earlier printed formula. The Theorem 15 numbering is that of the inspected Aichholzer arXiv text.

value.rationale: The complete-graph matching flip metric and its sphere counts concern a natural object, and the explicit formula is a useful presentation. But the exact fact sought is a direct weighted restatement of the known orbital counts and complete-graph component metric. Its radius, diameter and top-layer numbers follow from the same weights and do not supply an independent gap. There is no supported distinct valuable remainder in the frozen result; no repaired finding is submitted.
residual_risks: The decision does not rule on other statistics, such as multiplicities of shortest flip sequences, which are not claimed or derived here.
